definition: One or more data sets plus, where relevant, the data services used to access them.
A structured collection of data selected and organised for a defined outcome or need. It can be a subset of a larger system.
A controlled means of accessing one or more data sets, such as an API or secure access mechanism.
A specific representation of a data set, for example a CSV file or a feed.

alt_labels: CDA; essential shared data asset; ESDA
definition: A data asset shared across government where losing access could stop an organisation from fulfilling important functions. 'Essential shared data asset' is the older term it replaced.
Data one organisation gives to another to support an essential process or purpose the receiver is responsible for.
Data one organisation obtains from another to support an essential process or purpose it is responsible for.
One of the seven reasons a critical data asset matters, such as public service delivery or official statistics. Each asset supports at least one.
The conditions an asset must meet to be in scope of the policy: classified OFFICIAL, critical, and within the provider's ownership accountabilities.
Information that describes a data asset so it can be found, understood, validated, reused and shared.
A managed collection of metadata records that helps people and systems find, understand and reuse data assets. It holds descriptions, not the data.
The W3C vocabulary for describing data sets and data services in catalogues, so catalogues can be harvested and searched together.
The UK cross-government model, based on DCAT, for the metadata exchanged about data assets.
The GDS service being scoped to link to departments' own catalogues and make critical data asset metadata discoverable across government.

alt_labels: CDA return; baseline return; annual return
definition: An organisation's report of its in-scope assets and their metadata to GDS, assured by the department for its ALBs.
A senior leader accountable for the meaning, content, quality and management of a data asset.
The role accountable to the SIRO for protecting the whole information asset. Related to, but not the same as, the data owner.
The role running an asset day to day: standards, access, quality processes and documentation.
The technical expert for the system holding the data: storage, access controls, auditable change and disposal.
A defined set of accountabilities for data. Records name roles, not people.
The choice between keeping the IAO model, adopting the data ownership model, or a hybrid. Each must still meet the mandatory IAO actions.
One of the five repeatable governance activities: Mandate, Frame, Assign, Operate, Assure.
A one-page statement of a governance body's purpose, scope, authority and review cadence.
A running record of governance decisions: what, who, why, when and the review trigger.
A logged, time-bound deviation from policy with an owner and an expiry date. An exception without an expiry is an undocumented policy change.
Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed. One accountable role per activity.
The plan every identified asset must have, or an equivalent mechanism, for managing its quality across seven steps.
A data item whose quality drives the most important decisions made with the asset.
A measurable aspect of quality. The framework's six are completeness, uniqueness, consistency, timeliness, validity and accuracy.
The GDS method that scores importance times impact to set targets, and uses the band below target to set priority and time to resolve.
A plain-English summary of an asset's quality, known issues and what it should not be used for.
The W3C vocabulary for publishing quality measurements with a catalogue record.
Quality rules and promises written down as a file that suppliers and users share.
An organisation's capability around data, self-assessed with the government framework.
The person each organisation nominates to coordinate DAM Policy adoption and the return, and to sit on the Working Group.
